overview: This file traces the recovery, capacity, and allocation of Japan’s pulp, paper, and especially newsprint industries under the Allied occupation from 1947 through 1949. It combines production reports and statistical tables prepared by SCAP’s Natural Resources and Economic and Scientific Sections with State Department despatches on mill capacity, shortages of pulpwood, coal, chemicals, and electricity, and the loss of prewar raw-material sources. A second major strand concerns the politically contentious rationing of scarce newsprint, including American Federation of Labor allegations that Communist publications received preferential treatment, SCAP’s detailed rebuttal, and a later political-party allocation plan. The opening telegram about a Siamese textile-purchasing mission appears to have been included through a cross-reference rather than because it concerns paper manufacturing directly.

subfiles.title: Telegram approving a Siamese textile mission to Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo, for the U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.about: The Department approves the entry into Japan of two Siamese representatives seeking to arrange the purchase and shipment of Japanese textiles.
subfiles.summary: State approves a Siamese mission's entry to negotiate textile shipments to Bangkok with SCAP, pending SCAP agreement.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1023 on February–March pulp and paper production
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch reports improving Japanese pulp and paper output and supplies March 1947 production statistics requested by the Department of Commerce.
subfiles.summary: Report: Japan's March 1947 paper and pulp production hit new occupation-era highs, credited to cooperation rather than coercion with industry.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice for Despatch No. 1108
subfiles.to: Department of State action office and DC/R
subfiles.about: This administrative sheet designates the attached copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 1108 as the record copy replacing an unreturned original.
subfiles.summary: Record-copy sheet replaces a lost despatch on newsprint, filed for permanent record in 1948.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1108 transmitting “Newsprint in Japan”
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a SCAP preliminary study of Japan’s newsprint industry.
subfiles.summary: Despatch transmits SCAP's study on Japanese newsprint history, mills, forest resources, and trade statistics.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1223/1283 transmitting March–May production reports
subfiles.from: Counselor of Mission, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards two Natural Resources Section memoranda on Japanese pulp and paper production in March, April, and May 1947.
subfiles.summary: Despatch extends Japan's pulp and paper production data through May 1947.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on March–April 1947 pulp and paper production
subfiles.from: Harold R. Murdock, Natural Resources Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.about: The memorandum explains apparent April production declines caused by altered reporting periods and compares March and April pulp and paper output.
subfiles.summary: Report: April 1947 figures show Japan shifting from newsprint toward other printing papers, with rayon pulp and unbleached kraft output rising.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on April–May 1947 pulp and paper production
subfiles.from: Harold R. Murdock, Natural Resources Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.about: The memorandum compares April and May output and examines a sharp May decline in rayon pulp production.
subfiles.summary: Report: May 1947 rayon pulp output fell sharply, blamed on coal and power shortages, though total pulp and paper output still rose.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 119 surveying 1947 newsprint production, exports, and imports
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch responds to a circular inquiry with estimates of Japan’s effective, installed, and near-term newsprint capacity.
subfiles.summary: SCAP estimates Japan's effective newsprint capacity at 175,000 tons, with 1948 output likely only 75% of that.

subfiles.title: State Department inquiry about alleged pro-Communist newsprint allocations
subfiles.from: U.S. Department of State, signed George C. Marshall
subfiles.to: SCAP, Tokyo, for the Acting U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.about: The Department requests information and comment on Matthew Woll’s accusation that scarce Japanese newsprint was being distributed disproportionately to Communist publications and unions.
subfiles.summary: State asks SCAP to justify newsprint allocations to the Communist Red Flag and other outlets, after an AFL complaint of favoritism.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on newsprint allocations to Communist and labor publications
subfiles.to: Department of the Army and U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.about: SCAP explains and defends Japan’s newsprint allocation system while outlining contemplated reallocations and additional supplies for labor-union publications.
subfiles.summary: SCAP defends Communist-paper Akahata's small newsprint share as generous relative to party strength, fearing a cut would stir sympathy, and plans a union-newsprint allocation.

subfiles.title: SCAP telegram on 1948 newsprint statistics and the 1949 forecast
subfiles.to: Department of the Army, for passage to the U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: The telegram supplies Japanese newsprint capacity, production, trade, and forecast figures requested for calendar year 1948.
subfiles.summary: SCAP reports 1948 newsprint output below capacity, no exports, and lost prewar pulpwood sources now hurting 1949 production.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 259 on political-party newsprint allocations
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch reports a proposed newsprint-allocation plan for Japanese political-party publications, apparently intended to begin on May 1, 1949.
subfiles.summary: Damaged despatch concerns a new political-party newsprint allocation plan under a Newsprint Allocations Board.

interest: Shows postwar Japan's paper-industry recovery and newsprint rationing entangled with anti-Communist politics.
